choices: To demo the product to stakeholders
To plan ways to improve quality and effectiveness
explanation: The team inspects how the Sprint went with people, process and tools, and picks improvements. The demo happens in the Sprint Review.

subject: scrum
prompt: Which best describes the Scrum Master?
choices: The project manager who assigns work
A leader who serves the team and the organization
The person who writes the requirements
explanation: The Scrum Master is accountable for the team's effectiveness and for Scrum being understood. They coach and remove impediments.

subject: scrum
prompt: Who decides how many backlog items to take into a Sprint?
explanation: Only the people doing the work can judge how much they can finish.

subject: scrum
prompt: The idea that knowledge comes from experience, and that decisions should rest on what is observed, is called ___.
explanation: Scrum is founded on empiricism and lean thinking. Empiricism is why Scrum keeps inspecting real results instead of trusting a long up-front plan.

subject: scrum
prompt: Match each Scrum value to what it asks of the team.
extras: Reach the goals and support each other
Put the work of the Sprint first
Be honest about work and challenges
See teammates as capable and independent
Do the right thing on tough problems
explanation: Each value is described in the Scrum Guide by the behaviour it asks for. Together they guide the team's work, actions and behaviour.

subject: scrum
prompt: When a Scrum Team and the people it works with live the five values, what do the three pillars build?
explanation: The Guide says that when the values are embodied, transparency, inspection and adaptation come to life and build trust.

subject: scrum
prompt: A Scrum Team that decides internally who does what, when and how is called self-___.
explanation: Scrum Teams are self-managing and cross-functional. Cross-functional is the other trait: the team has all the skills needed to create value each Sprint.

subject: scrum
prompt: The Developers are stuck because another department is slow to grant access to a system. What is the Scrum Master's part?
choices: Reassign the blocked work to other Developers
Cause the impediment to be removed
Lengthen the Sprint by a week
explanation: Serving the Scrum Team includes causing the removal of impediments to its progress. Assigning work is up to the self-managing team, only the Product Owner can cancel a Sprint, and Sprint length is fixed.

subject: scrum
prompt: What does the Scrum Master do about the Scrum events?
choices: Sets the agenda of every Daily Scrum
Makes sure they take place, stay productive and keep to their timebox
Attends only when the Product Owner asks
Approves the outcome of each event
explanation: The Scrum Master ensures all events happen, are positive and productive, and stay within the timebox. The Developers choose how to run their own Daily Scrum.

subject: scrum
prompt: Put the events inside one Sprint in the order they happen.
explanation: Planning opens the Sprint, the Daily Scrum is held each working day, the Review is second to last and the Retrospective closes the Sprint. The decoys are not Scrum events.

subject: scrum
prompt: Sprint Planning covers three topics: why this Sprint is valuable, what can be Done this Sprint, and ___ the chosen work will get done.
explanation: Why leads to the Sprint Goal, what is the selection of Product Backlog items, and how is the Developers' plan. Together they form the Sprint Backlog.

subject: scrum
prompt: What must be finalized before Sprint Planning ends?
choices: A size for every Product Backlog item
The agenda of the Sprint Review
explanation: The whole Scrum Team defines a Sprint Goal that says why the Sprint is valuable to stakeholders, and it must be settled before Planning is over.

subject: scrum
prompt: During Product Backlog refinement, who is responsible for sizing the items?
choices: The Developers who will do the work
explanation: The people who will do the work size it. The Product Owner can influence them by helping them understand and choose trade-offs.

subject: scrum
prompt: A Sprint Backlog holds the Sprint Goal (why), the selected Product Backlog items (what) and a ___ for delivering the Increment (how).
explanation: Why, what and how: the goal, the selected items and an actionable plan. The Sprint Backlog is a plan by and for the Developers and is updated throughout the Sprint.

subject: scrum
prompt: A Product Backlog item does not meet the Definition of Done when the Sprint ends. What happens to it?
choices: It is shown at the Sprint Review as almost finished
It is released with a warning
It returns to the Product Backlog for future consideration
It moves automatically into the next Sprint Backlog
explanation: Work that is not Done is not part of the Increment. It cannot be released or even presented at the Sprint Review, and it goes back to the Product Backlog.

subject: scrum
prompt: Match each event to its timebox for a one-month Sprint.
explanation: Shorter Sprints usually have shorter events. The Daily Scrum is always 15 minutes.

subject: scrum
prompt: Match each artifact to its commitment.
explanation: Each artifact has a commitment that gives it focus and makes progress measurable.

subject: scrum
prompt: A team inspects its work at every event but never changes anything afterwards. How does Scrum theory see that inspection?
choices: As enough, because the work stayed visible
As pointless, because inspection exists to enable adaptation
As the Product Owner's problem only
As correct, because plans should stay fixed
explanation: The pillars build on each other: transparency enables inspection, and inspection enables adaptation. Inspecting without adapting achieves nothing.

subject: scrum
prompt: A team keeps Sprints and a Product Backlog but drops the Sprint Retrospective for good. What does the Scrum Guide say about using only parts of Scrum?
choices: It is fine as long as the team delivers
It is possible, but the result is not Scrum
It is allowed once the Scrum Master approves
It is required for small teams
explanation: The Guide treats the framework as a whole. Leaving out an element is possible, but what remains is not Scrum, and it hides problems the missing part would have shown.

subject: scrum
prompt: Halfway through a Sprint, the Scrum Team tells its stakeholders plainly that the work has hit a serious problem. Which Scrum value is this the clearest example of?
explanation: Openness is the team and its stakeholders being open about the work and the challenges. Hiding the problem would also damage transparency.

subject: scrum
prompt: The Product Owner asks a colleague to write and order the Product Backlog items. Who is accountable for the Product Backlog now?
explanation: The Product Owner may delegate the work of managing the backlog, but stays accountable for it. The Product Owner is one person, not a committee.

subject: scrum
prompt: Match each Scrum Master service to the group that receives it.
answers: Finding techniques for Product Backlog management
explanation: The Scrum Master serves three groups. Coaching team members is for the Scrum Team, backlog techniques are for the Product Owner, and guiding adoption is for the whole organization.

subject: scrum
prompt: How does the Scrum Guide treat burn-down charts?
choices: As a useful practice that does not replace empiricism
As the commitment of the Sprint Backlog
As something Scrum Teams must not use
explanation: The Guide names burn-downs, burn-ups and cumulative flows as practices for forecasting progress. They can help, but only what has already happened can inform decisions. Scrum's three artifacts are the Product Backlog, Sprint Backlog and Increment.

subject: scrum
prompt: The Product Owner is actively working on an item in the Sprint Backlog. How do they take part in the Daily Scrum?
explanation: The Daily Scrum belongs to the Developers. A Product Owner or Scrum Master who is actively working on Sprint Backlog items participates as a Developer.

subject: scrum
prompt: Which statement about the Sprint Review matches the Scrum Guide?
choices: It is a formal gate that must approve every release
It is a working session where the Scrum Team and stakeholders decide what to do next
It is a private meeting of the Developers
It is where the team inspects its own process and tools
explanation: At the Review the team presents its results to key stakeholders, and together they discuss progress toward the Product Goal and what to do next. It should not be only a presentation, and it is not a release gate. Inspecting process and tools is the Retrospective.

subject: scrum
prompt: Midway through a Sprint the Developers find the work is much larger than they expected. What does the Scrum Guide have them do?
choices: Change the Sprint Goal to match
Negotiate the scope of the Sprint Backlog with the Product Owner
Ask the Scrum Master to extend the Sprint
explanation: Scope can be renegotiated with the Product Owner without affecting the Sprint Goal. Quality must not drop, and a Sprint's length is fixed.

subject: scrum
prompt: An organization has a Definition of Done as part of its standards. What must its Scrum Teams do?
choices: Ignore it and write their own
Follow it only if the Product Owner agrees
explanation: An organizational Definition of Done is the minimum every Scrum Team follows. If there is no such standard, the Scrum Team creates a definition that suits its product.

subject: scrum
prompt: Put the journey of one Product Backlog item in order, from the backlog to the stakeholders' eyes.
answers: Product Owner orders it in the Product Backlog
Developers select it in Sprint Planning
It meets the Definition of Done
It is presented at the Sprint Review
extras: Stakeholders sign off the Sprint Backlog
explanation: An item is ordered by the Product Owner, selected by the Developers, and becomes part of an Increment the moment it meets the Definition of Done. Only Done work is presented at the Review. No approval step by the Scrum Master exists.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: A company buys cyber insurance. Which risk response is that?
explanation: Insurance shifts the financial impact to another party.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: What is the core idea of zero trust?
choices: Never trust, always verify every request
explanation: Being inside the network earns no trust. Every user and device is checked each time.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: What does hashing a file mainly let you verify?
explanation: If the hash matches, the file hasn't changed. A hash keeps nothing secret.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: Match each risk response to an example.
extras: Document the risk and carry on
Add a control to reduce it
explanation: The four standard ways to treat a risk.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: Which metric is the maximum amount of data, measured in time, that a business can afford to lose?
explanation: Recovery Point Objective sets how often you must back up. RTO is how fast you must be running again.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: Reviewing audit logs after the fact is which type of control?
explanation: Detective controls find events that have already happened. A firewall rule is preventive, and restoring a backup is corrective.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: A phishing email aimed specifically at a company's CEO is called:
explanation: Whaling targets senior executives. Vishing uses voice calls and smishing uses text messages.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: What does a SIEM do?
choices: Collects and correlates logs from many systems to spot incidents
explanation: Security Information and Event Management gives one place to search, correlate and alert on events.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: Which key creates a digital signature?
explanation: Only the sender holds the private key, so anyone can check the signature with the public key and know who signed.

subject: securityPlus
prompt: Put the incident response phases in order.
explanation: Stop the spread before you clean up, and always finish by reviewing what happened.

subject: aws
prompt: Which AWS service is object storage?
explanation: Simple Storage Service stores files as objects in buckets.

subject: aws
prompt: What is an Availability Zone?
choices: One or more data centers within a Region
explanation: A Region contains several isolated Availability Zones. Spreading across them protects against one site failing.

subject: aws
prompt: What should you do with the AWS root user?
choices: Turn on MFA and use it only for the few tasks that need it
explanation: The root user can do anything, so lock it away and work through IAM users or roles with limited permissions.

subject: aws
prompt: What is a VPC?
choices: A logically isolated virtual network for your resources
explanation: Virtual Private Cloud gives you your own address range, subnets and routing.

subject: aws
prompt: Match each service to what it does.
explanation: Five of the most commonly tested core services.

subject: aws
prompt: Under the shared responsibility model, what is always the customer's job?
choices: Their own data and who can access it
explanation: AWS secures the cloud itself. You secure what you put in it: data, identities and configuration.

subject: aws
prompt: Which service records the API calls made in your account?
explanation: CloudTrail is the audit log of who did what. CloudWatch is for metrics, logs and alarms.

subject: aws
prompt: Your workload can be interrupted at any time and you want the lowest price. Which EC2 option fits?
explanation: Spot uses spare capacity at a large discount, but AWS can reclaim it at short notice.

subject: aws
prompt: Which is a managed NoSQL key-value database?
explanation: DynamoDB is serverless NoSQL. RDS runs relational engines, and Redshift is a data warehouse.

subject: azure
prompt: What is Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure Active Directory)?
choices: A cloud identity and access service
explanation: It handles sign-in, single sign-on and multi-factor authentication.

subject: azure
prompt: What is a resource group?
choices: A logical container for related resources
explanation: Every resource lives in exactly one resource group, which makes it easy to manage or delete them together.

subject: azure
prompt: Which Azure service is object storage for files and images?
explanation: Blob stands for binary large object.

subject: azure
prompt: What is Azure Key Vault for?
explanation: Keeping secrets in a vault keeps them out of source code and configuration files.

subject: azure
prompt: Moving to the cloud shifts spending mainly from:
explanation: You stop buying hardware up front (capital expense) and pay for what you use (operating expense).

subject: azure
prompt: Match each service to its cloud model.
explanation: With IaaS you manage the operating system. With PaaS you manage only your app. With SaaS you just use the software.

subject: azure
prompt: Match each AWS service to its closest Azure counterpart.
explanation: The big clouds offer similar building blocks under different names.

subject: azure
prompt: You must stop anyone creating resources outside two approved regions. Which tool enforces that?
explanation: Policy governs what resources may look like. RBAC governs who may do what.

subject: azure
prompt: Order the Azure management levels from top to bottom.
explanation: Policies and permissions set at a higher level are inherited by everything below.

subject: history
prompt: In 1997, IBM's Deep Blue made headlines by:
choices: Beating world chess champion Garry Kasparov

subject: history
prompt: Type the year the Linux kernel was first released.
explanation: Torvalds announced it in August 1991 and released version 0.01 that September.

subject: history
prompt: Match each person to what they are known for.
extras: Designing the Apple I and II
explanation: Five people whose work shaped modern computing.

subject: history
prompt: Claude Shannon's 1948 paper "A Mathematical Theory of Communication" founded which field?
explanation: It defined how to measure information and the limits of sending it over a noisy channel.

subject: history
prompt: What was Microsoft's first product, in 1975?
choices: A BASIC interpreter for the Altair 8800
explanation: Bill Gates and Paul Allen wrote Altair BASIC before the company had its name.

subject: history
prompt: Which operating system did Microsoft supply for the 1981 IBM PC?
choices: MS-DOS (sold by IBM as PC DOS)
explanation: Microsoft kept the right to license DOS to other PC makers, which made it the industry standard.

subject: history
prompt: Besides Linux, which widely used tool did Linus Torvalds create in 2005?
explanation: He wrote Git to manage Linux kernel development.

subject: history
prompt: Where did Apple's team see the graphical interface ideas that inspired the Lisa and Macintosh?
explanation: Xerox's Alto had windows, icons and a mouse. Apple refined those ideas for a consumer product.

subject: history

explanation: Five milestones in under fifty years.

subject: history
prompt: What did Claude Shannon's 1937 master's thesis show?
choices: Boolean algebra can describe and design switching circuits
Programs can be stored in memory
explanation: It connected true/false logic to on/off switches, the basis of digital circuit design.

subject: history
prompt: Why was the IBM System/360 (1964) a turning point?
choices: It was a family of compatible computers that ran the same software
It was the first personal computer
explanation: Customers could upgrade to a bigger model without rewriting their programs, an idea that shaped the industry.
